bullets.title: Fed hawkishness dominates: Waller floats 50bp Dec hike, curve flattens 6bp
bullets.body: FOMC minutes showed almost all participants see further hikes appropriate; Gov. Waller explicitly advocated a 50bp December hike and reversal of 2025 cuts, warning markets may need to be 'shocked' if the Fed doesn't signal a January hike. Morgan Stanley maintains a 25bp base case with a high bar for 50bp unless payrolls are very strong. The 2yr sits at 4.800% and 10yr at 5.064% as the curve twist-flattened 6bp.

bullets.title: 10yr Treasury approaching highest auction yield since 2002; TIPS real yields +22bp
bullets.body: 10yr real yields rose 22bp net of carry since the last TIPS auction, with breakevens appearing 2+ standard errors cheap to fair value. The upcoming 10yr TIPS auction would clear at the highest yield since 2002 if priced at current levels; 10yr auctions have tailed in 15 of the last 17 since 2024. T-bill projections show -$216bn net paydowns between Dec 3 and Jan 12.

bullets.title: All major US indices below 200-day MAs; market breadth deteriorating
bullets.body: SPX, CCMP, DJIA, MID, and RTY all broke below their 200-day moving averages. One macro strategist targets S&P 7,000 and VIX 40 before covering shorts, citing significant technical damage; 65% of the Russell 3000 is already in a bear market. Copper, gold, oil, and semiconductors declining together signal a potential slowdown, with the dollar index near 104.

bullets.title: NVDA FY28 guidance +75% fails to sustain AI trade bounce; multiple overhangs weigh
bullets.body: NVDA beat Q3 and raised FY28 revenue growth guidance to ~75% from ~70% with demand exceeding supply, but the stock fell ~2.9% as multiple headwinds offset the print: the board has not reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO (ARM's Rene Haas approached), Congress is probing chip diversion to China, the SEC opened a civil probe, and Hopper/H200 sales to China were halted. Anthropic's IPO (reported 5-6x oversubscribed at $83/share, ~$1.4T implied valuation) adds near-term supply pressure.

bullets.title: Retail earnings broadly strong; AI-driven conversion gains and fuel/freight headwinds emerge as 2H themes
bullets.body: TJX (+4% comp, +100bps vs guidance), TGT (+5.6% comp, raised FY), and Home Depot (+2.2% comp) all beat. AI tools are becoming a measurable driver: Lowe's Mylow triples online conversion, Target's Ask Target doubles purchase rates, and HD's AI search produced 6 straight quarters of double-digit online comp growth. Fuel/freight is the offsetting headwind — TJX guided 50bp GM drag, Lowe's cited diesel +15% vs Q2 for ~30bp GM pressure, and HD flagged unplanned inflation in energy/resin/metals at -60bp GM y/y.

bullets.title: NVDA executing $150B buyback authorization at ~$45B/qtr; supporting supply-chain financing
bullets.body: NVDA is running buybacks at roughly 2x its historical quarterly average through end-FY28, while also prioritizing $118B in supplier capital support and data center land/power/shell guarantees ($105B credit support). This positions NVDA as a de facto financing arm of the AI ecosystem — described as 'tightening so the FOMC doesn't have to.'

bullets.title: Retail flows: crypto ETF liquidations funding equity ETF dips; net equity supply ~$270bn in 2026
bullets.body: JPM estimates net equity supply at ~$270bn in 2026, the first positive reading since the 2021 IPO boom, implying a ~4.5% return drag. Retail investors have been buying equity ETF dips in July, October, and November but are funding purchases by heavily selling crypto ETFs over the past two weeks. Bitcoin has fallen to ~$65k vs an estimated $86k production cost.

bullets.title: Housing data weakens: permits fall 7.4% m/m to cycle lows; pending sales miss
bullets.body: October housing starts came in at 1,309K SAAR (above 1,270K consensus) but building permits plunged 7.4% m/m to a fresh cycle low, with single-family starts down ~9%. Pending home sales fell 4.7% m/m vs -1.8% forecast. Elevated mortgage rates (30yr at 7.46%) and rate volatility are cited as the demand headwall; Home Depot and Lowe's both flagged elevated rates as a 2027 demand headwind.

bullets.title: Data center construction fell 28% in Q3; permitting moratoria spreading across states
bullets.body: US data center construction starts fell 28% Q3 (8.4GW) from Q2's record 11.7GW; total pipeline ~58GW vs 65.1GW operating capacity. Loudon County, VA adopted a 12-month pause; nine states have policy-driven construction delays. Texas TCEQ resumed air permits Nov 17 (Wells Fargo estimates 0.5-3.5GW of behind-the-meter projects could advance). OpenAI's $20B Georgia campus received preliminary approval.

bullets.title: AI optimism supports REITs and infrastructure equities despite broader market weakness
bullets.body: S&P 500 RE Index outperformed (+0.17%) with Data Center REITs +0.50% and YTD +27.34%. Office REITs (+1.19%) also gained, with Goldman positive on West Coast office trends (KRC +2.7%). US high-street retail rents +5.8% YTD vs +3.4% prior year; NYC Fifth Avenue rents +35% YTD to ~$2,700/sqft.

bullets.title: Foreign Treasury demand softening: officials shed $23.7bn in T-bills; foreign T-bill ownership at record low 4.1%
bullets.body: Foreign investors net bought $80.8bn in long-term Treasuries in September, but foreign officials simultaneously shed $23.7bn in short-term Treasuries, pushing foreign T-bill ownership to a record low 4.1%. Primary dealer positions in 6-11yr sector are in line with July levels, limiting natural demand at the upcoming 10yr TIPS auction.

bullets.title: Micron: 75% of 2027 supply already committed; 2027-28 expected tighter than record 2026
bullets.body: At TomorrowX, Micron noted AI-driven memory demand is robust with 75% of 2027 supply sold out and 2028 customer discussions already underway. The company expects 2027 to be stronger than record 2026, and 2027-28 even tighter, underpinned by multiyear take-or-pay agreements with ~5-year terms. Stacked 3D DRAM is flagged as the next major wave, entering market ~2028-29 and proliferating by 2030-31.

bullets.title: BoE Bailey flags data dependency; AI contribution to UK GDP growth fading in 4Q
bullets.body: BoE Governor Bailey emphasized a meeting-by-meeting approach given volatile inflation drivers; softer labor/inflation data and lower energy prices reduce urgency for a December hike (February now more likely). Notably, BoE's AI activity proxy shows the AI build-out accounted for ~20% of 2026 UK GDP growth YTD, but that contribution tailed off in August-September with direct growth boost expected to weaken in 4Q.

bullets.title: Goldman screens: 38 non-tech Russell 1000 stocks citing AI revenue lift; buyback aristocrats at fair value
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs identified 38 non-technology Russell 1000 companies discussing AI-boosted revenues (including FDS, MDT, NDAQ, PAYX) and 38 with above-average physical presence citing AI productivity gains. Buyback aristocrats historically outperform when growth decelerates; they currently trade at only a 2% P/E premium to the equal-weight S&P 500, near historical average — suggesting the trade is not crowded.

bullets.title: US hotel RevPAR surged +12.9% YOY for Nov 8-14; luxury +15.5%, upper upscale +11.7%
bullets.body: Weekly US RevPAR accelerated to +12.9% YOY from +4.7% the prior week (easier comps from 2025 government shutdown), with trailing 28-day up +10.0%. Luxury led at +15.5%, economy at +10.9%. Top 25 markets up +14.2%; Miami +32.2%, San Francisco +24.8%, Chicago +24.8%. 4Q26 tracking for C-corps ahead of consensus: HLT +8.1% vs +4.5%, MAR +7.9% vs +5.9%.

bullets.title: Congress likely to pass AI Overwatch Act and Chip Security Act by year-end; chip diversion probe escalates
bullets.body: A Congressional report flagged China's military seeking advanced Nvidia chips for AI-enabled weapons, triggering an active investigation into chip diversion. Legislation targeting chip access to China (AI Overwatch Act, Chip Security Act) is expected by year-end or early 2027. Nvidia halted Hopper/H200 sales to China in response.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO: ~$500B in orders, priced at $83/share; ~$1.4T implied valuation raises sustainability questions
bullets.body: Anthropic's IPO attracted nearly $500B in investor orders and is upsizing. At ~$1.4T implied valuation, the company would need ~$350B in annual revenue at a 20% FCF margin — vs a current ~$80B run rate — to justify the price. Avory CIO Emory notes 80% of Anthropic revenue comes from models launched within 6 months, making it vulnerable to OpenAI and open-weight competition, and the company faces ~$900B in compute commitments over a decade.

bullets.title: Compute futures market emerging: Compute Desk raises $45M; CFTC decision expected January
bullets.body: Compute Desk raised a $45M seed round (led by Lightspeed) to build capital markets infrastructure for GPU capacity as a tradable commodity — including price indexes, a liquidity network, and physical-settlement clearing. The team draws from Citadel/Two Sigma, Winton, and Meta/AWS. CFTC approval is expected in early January; hyperscalers including Meta already use Compute Signal for price assessments.

bullets.title: FOMC minutes: 'almost all' see more hikes appropriate; only 'a couple' considered 50bp for December
bullets.body: The October FOMC hold reflected the value of awaiting more data alongside doubts about AI productivity, tighter financial conditions, and uncertainty over prior September hike effects. Only a couple of participants discussed a 50bp December move. The minutes' focus on financial conditions gave the overall tone a slightly dovish read relative to Waller's subsequent hawkish comments.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley favors Japan and Korea vs EM/China for 2027; above-average volatility expected
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Asia EM strategy maintains overweights in Japan and Korea over EM broadly and China specifically heading into 2027, expecting the secular earnings cycle to continue with significant upside to targets. Above-average volatility is anticipated across the region.
